title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Geometric Twins
text:
Geometric Twins

Key terms: congruent, shape, size

Geometric twins are figures that have the same shape and size. They can be superimposed exactly, one over the other. To recreate a figure, we need to take measurements that fix its shape and size.

text:
Congruent Figures

Key terms: congruent, shape, size

Congruent figures are figures that have the same shape and size. They can be superimposed exactly, one over the other. This means that their corresponding sides and angles are equal.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | SSS (Side Side Side) Condition
text:
SSS (Side Side Side) Condition

Key terms: SSS, congruent, triangle

The SSS condition states that if two triangles have the same three side lengths, then they are congruent. This means that we can recreate a triangle exactly if we know its three side lengths.

metadata.subject: Mathematics

text:

Key terms: SAS, congruent, triangle

The SAS condition states that if two triangles have the same two side lengths and the included angle, then they are congruent. This means that we can recreate a triangle exactly if we know two of its side lengths and the included angle.

metadata.subject: Mathematics

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | ASA (Angle Side Angle) Condition
text:
ASA (Angle Side Angle) Condition

Key terms: ASA, congruent, triangle

The ASA condition states that if two triangles have the same two angles and the included side, then they are congruent. This means that we can recreate a triangle exactly if we know two of its angles and the included side.

SSA (Side Side Angle) Condition

Key terms: SSA, congruent, triangle

The SSA condition states that if two triangles have the same two side lengths and a non-included angle, then they may or may not be congruent. This means that we cannot always recreate a triangle exactly if we know two of its side lengths and a non-included angle.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Addition
text:
Integer Addition

Key terms: integer, addition, number line, token model

Integer addition involves combining two or more integers to get a sum. When adding integers, we can use the number line or the token model to help us. The number line shows that adding two integers with the same sign (both positive or both negative) results in a positive sum, while adding two integers with different signs results in a negative sum. The token model uses positive and negative tokens to represent integers and helps us visualize the process of adding integers.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Addition in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Subtraction
text:
Integer Subtraction

Key terms: integer, subtraction, additive inverse

Integer subtraction involves finding the difference between two integers. We can use the number line or the token model to help us. When subtracting integers, we can think of it as adding the opposite (or additive inverse) of the second integer to the first integer. For example, 7 - 3 can be thought of as 7 + (-3).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Subtraction in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Multiplication of Integers
text:
Multiplication of Integers

Key terms: integer, multiplication, token model

Integer multiplication involves finding the product of two integers. We can use the token model to help us. When multiplying integers, we can think of it as adding the first integer a certain number of times, equal to the second integer. For example, 4 × 3 can be thought of as adding 4 together 3 times.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Multiplication of Integers in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Patterns in Integer Multiplication
text:
Patterns in Integer Multiplication

Key terms: integer, multiplication, patterns

When multiplying integers, we can observe certain patterns. When the multiplicand is positive, for every unit decrease in the multiplier, the product decreases by the multiplicand. When the multiplicand is negative, for every unit decrease in the multiplier, the product increases by the multiplicand. These patterns continue even when the multiplier is negative.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Patterns in Integer Multiplication in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Properties of Integer Multiplication
text:
Properties of Integer Multiplication

Key terms: integer, multiplication, properties

When multiplying integers, we can observe certain properties. The magnitude of the product does not change with the change in signs of the multiplier and the multiplicand. When both the multiplier and the multiplicand are positive, the product is positive. When both the multiplier and the multiplicand are negative, the product is positive. When one of the multiplier or the multiplicand is positive and the other is negative, their product is negative.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Properties of Integer Multiplication in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Swapping Multiplier and Multiplicand
text:
Swapping Multiplier and Multiplicand

Key terms: integer, multiplication, swapping

When multiplying integers, we can swap the multiplier and the multiplicand. The magnitude of the product does not change when the multiplier and the multiplicand are swapped. However, the sign of the product may change if we swap the multiplier and the multiplicand.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Swapping Multiplier and Multiplicand in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Additive Inverse in Integer Multiplication
text:
Additive Inverse in Integer Multiplication

Key terms: integer, multiplication, additive inverse

In integer multiplication, the additive inverse of the multiplicand is used. The additive inverse of an integer 'a' is represented as -a. When multiplying an integer by -1, the product is the additive inverse of the multiplicand.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Additive Inverse in Integer Multiplication in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Token Model for Integer Operations
text:
Token Model for Integer Operations

The token model is a visual representation of integers and their operations. It uses positive and negative tokens to represent integers and helps us visualize the process of adding and multiplying integers.

metadata.subject: Mathematics

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Multiplication Commutative Property
text:
Integer Multiplication Commutative Property

Key terms: commutative, property, multiplication

The order of integers being multiplied does not change the product. For example, 3 × 4 = 4 × 3.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Multiplication Commutative Property in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Multiplication Associative Property
text:
Integer Multiplication Associative Property

Key terms: associative, property, multiplication

When multiplying three integers, the order in which they are multiplied does not change the product. For example, (2 × 3) × 4 = 2 × (3 × 4).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Multiplication Associative Property in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Multiplication Distributive Property
text:
Integer Multiplication Distributive Property

Key terms: distributive, property, multiplication

The distributive property allows us to multiply a single integer by the sum of two integers. For example, 2 × (3 + 4) = 2 × 3 + 2 × 4.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Multiplication Distributive Property in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Sign of Integer Product
text:
Sign of Integer Product

Key terms: sign, product, integer

The product of two integers is positive if both integers are positive or both are negative. The product is negative if one integer is positive and the other is negative.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sign of Integer Product in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Integer Division Rules
text:
Integer Division Rules

Key terms: division, rules, integer

When dividing two integers, the quotient is positive if both the dividend and divisor are positive or both are negative. The quotient is negative if one integer is positive and the other is negative.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Integer Division Rules in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Brahmagupta's Rules for Integer Multiplication and Division
text:
Brahmagupta's Rules for Integer Multiplication and Division

Key terms: Brahmagupta, rules, multiplication, division

Brahmagupta's rules state that the product or quotient of two fortunes (positive integers) is a fortune, the product or quotient of two debts (negative integers) is a fortune, and the product or quotient of a debt and a fortune is a debt.

metadata.topic: Brahmagupta's Rules for Integer Multiplication and Division
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Brahmagupta's Rules for Integer Multiplication and Division in Grade 7 Mathematics.

Integer Division with Negative Numbers

text:
Integer Multiplication Properties

Key terms: commutative, associative, distributive

Integer multiplication is commutative, associative, and distributive over addition. This means that the order of the numbers doesn't change the result, and the multiplication can be grouped in different ways. These properties make it easier to work with integers and simplify calculations.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Terhüchü Game Rules
text:
Terhüchü Game Rules

Key terms: capture, jump, block

The goal of Terhüchü is to capture all the opponent's coins. Players take turns moving their coins along lines or jumping over opponent's coins to capture them. A player can also win by blocking their opponent's move or having more coins at the end of the game.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Terhüchü Game Rules in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Terhüchü Gameplay
text:
Terhüchü Gameplay

Key terms: move, jump, capture

Players can move their coins along lines or jump over opponent's coins to capture them. They can also skip empty intersections and move straight to the next one. Multiple captures in one move are allowed, and the direction can change after each jump.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Terhüchü Gameplay in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Finding HCF using factors
text:
Finding HCF using factors

Key terms: HCF, factors

To find the HCF of two numbers, list their factors and find the common factors. The HCF is the highest common factor. For example, the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, and the factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The common factors are 1, 2, and 4, so the HCF is 4.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Finding HCF using factors in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Highest Common Factor (HCF)
text:
Highest Common Factor (HCF)

Key terms: HCF, GCD

The HCF of two or more numbers is the highest common factor they have. It is also known as the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD). For example, the HCF of 12 and 16 is 4.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Highest Common Factor (HCF) in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Prime Factorisation
text:
Prime Factorisation

Key terms: prime factorisation

Prime factorisation is a way of breaking down a number into its prime factors. For example, the prime factorisation of 90 is 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. Prime factorisation can be used to find the HCF of two numbers.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Prime Factorisation in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Finding HCF using prime factorisation
text:
Finding HCF using prime factorisation

Key terms: HCF, prime factorisation

To find the HCF of two numbers using prime factorisation, list their prime factorisations and find the common prime factors. The HCF is the product of the common prime factors. For example, the prime factorisation of 45 is 3 × 3 × 5, and the prime factorisation of 75 is 3 × 5 × 5. The common prime factors are 3 and 5, so the HCF is 3 × 5 = 15.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Finding HCF using prime factorisation in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
text:
Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

Key terms: LCM

The LCM of two or more numbers is the lowest common multiple they have. It is the smallest number that is a multiple of all the given numbers. For example, the LCM of 6 and 8 is 24.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Finding LCM using multiples
text:
Finding LCM using multiples

Key terms: LCM, multiples

To find the LCM of two numbers using multiples, list the multiples of each number and find the smallest common multiple. For example, the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, ... and the multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, ... The smallest common multiple is 24.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Finding LCM using multiples in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Finding LCM using prime factorisation
text:
Finding LCM using prime factorisation

Key terms: LCM, prime factorisation

To find the LCM of two numbers using prime factorisation, list their prime factorisations and find the highest power of each prime factor. The LCM is the product of the highest powers of each prime factor. For example, the prime factorisation of 6 is 2 × 3, and the prime factorisation of 8 is 2 × 2 × 2. The highest power of 2 is 2 × 2 × 2, and the highest power of 3 is 3, so the LCM is 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Finding LCM using prime factorisation in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Common multiples
text:
Common multiples

Key terms: common multiples

Common multiples are numbers that are multiples of two or more given numbers. For example, the common multiples of 6 and 8 are 24, 48, 72, ...

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Common multiples in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Multiples and Factors
text:
Multiples and Factors

Key terms: multiples, factors

Multiples are numbers that can be divided by a given number. Factors are numbers that divide a given number without leaving a remainder. For example, the multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, etc. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Multiples and Factors in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Highest Common Factor (HCF)
text:
Highest Common Factor (HCF)

Key terms: HCF, common factors

The HCF of two or more numbers is the largest number that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder. To find the HCF, we need to find the common factors of the numbers and take the highest one. For example, the HCF of 12 and 18 is 6.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Highest Common Factor (HCF) in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Prime Factorisation
text:
Prime Factorisation

Key terms: prime factorisation, prime factors

Prime factorisation is the process of breaking down a number into its prime factors. Prime factors are numbers that can only be divided by 1 and themselves. For example, the prime factorisation of 12 is 2 × 2 × 3.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Prime Factorisation in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
text:
Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

Key terms: LCM, common multiples

The LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest number that is a multiple of each of the numbers. To find the LCM, we need to find the common multiples of the numbers and take the smallest one. For example, the LCM of 12 and 18 is 36.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Relationship between HCF and LCM
text:
Relationship between HCF and LCM

Key terms: HCF, LCM, product

The product of the HCF and LCM of two numbers is equal to the product of the two numbers. For example, the product of the HCF and LCM of 12 and 18 is 12 × 18 = 216.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Relationship between HCF and LCM in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Properties of HCF and LCM
text:
Properties of HCF and LCM

Key terms: HCF, LCM, properties

The HCF of two numbers is always less than or equal to the smaller number. The LCM of two numbers is always greater than or equal to the larger number. For example, the HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, which is less than 18. The LCM of 12 and 18 is 36, which is greater than 12.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Properties of HCF and LCM in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Finding HCF and LCM using Prime Factorisation
text:
Finding HCF and LCM using Prime Factorisation

Key terms: prime factorisation, HCF, LCM

We can find the HCF and LCM of two numbers by finding their prime factorisation and using the following rules: the HCF is the product of the common prime factors raised to the lowest power, and the LCM is the product of the common prime factors raised to the highest power.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Finding HCF and LCM using Prime Factorisation
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Finding HCF and LCM using Prime Factorisation in Grade 7 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Consecutive Numbers

Consecutive Numbers

Consecutive numbers are numbers that follow each other in order, like 1, 2, 3, or 10, 11, 12. They can be even or odd, and they can be any type of number. Consecutive numbers are often used in math problems and puzzles.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Consecutive Numbers in Grade 7 Mathematics.

HCF and LCM

The HCF (Highest Common Factor) and LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) are two important math concepts that help us find the greatest common divisor and the smallest common multiple of two or more numbers. We can use a procedure to find both HCF and LCM at the same time, making it quicker and easier.

Prime Numbers

Prime numbers are special numbers that can only be divided by 1 and themselves. For example, 2, 3, 5, and 7 are all prime numbers. Prime numbers are important in math and are used to find the factors of other numbers.

text:
Co-Prime Numbers

Key terms: co-prime, numbers

Co-prime numbers are numbers that have no common factors other than 1. For example, 8 and 15 are co-prime numbers because they have no common factors other than 1. Co-prime numbers are used in math to find the greatest common divisor and the smallest common multiple.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Math Terms
text:
Math Terms

Key terms: conjecture, generalisation

Math terms like 'conjecture' and 'generalisation' are used to describe math concepts and ideas. A conjecture is a statement that is believed to be true but has not been proven, while a generalisation is a statement that is true for all cases. Understanding these terms helps us communicate math ideas more effectively.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Decimals Basics
text:
Decimals Basics

Key terms: decimals, place value

Decimals are a natural extension of the Indian place value system to represent decimal fractions. They are used to represent quantities with a fractional part. For example, 27.53 refers to a quantity with 2 tens, 7 units, 5 tenths, and 3 hundredths.

Multiplying decimals is similar to multiplying fractions. To multiply two decimals, we multiply the numbers obtained by removing the decimal points and then place the decimal point appropriately based on the total number of zeroes in the denominator.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Dividing Decimals
text:
Dividing Decimals

Key terms: decimal division, fraction division

Dividing decimals is similar to dividing fractions. To divide a decimal by 1, 10, 100, 1000, and so on, we can just move the decimal point to the left by as many places as there are zeroes in the divisor.

Decimal Quotient

A decimal quotient is a result of dividing two numbers and getting a decimal answer. It can be obtained using division using place value or by converting the division to a fraction and then to a decimal.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Decimal Quotient in Grade 7 Mathematics.

text:
Fraction-Decimal Conversion

Fraction-decimal conversion involves converting a fraction to a decimal or vice versa. This can be done by dividing the numerator by the denominator or by multiplying the numerator and denominator by a common factor.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Fraction-Decimal Conversion in Grade 7 Mathematics.

Decimal Operations

text:
Tenths and Hundredths

Key terms: tenths, hundredths, decimal places

Tenths and hundredths are decimal places used to represent fractions of a whole. To divide numbers with tenths or hundredths, regroup them as needed and place a decimal point in the quotient. This process can be repeated to find decimal quotients.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Tenths and Hundredths in Grade 7 Mathematics.

text:

title: NCERT Grade 7 Mathematics | Solving Systems of Equations
text:
Solving Systems of Equations

Key terms: system, equation, variable

A system of equations is a set of two or more equations that have the same variables. To solve a system of equations, we need to find the values of the variables that satisfy all the equations. This can be done by using substitution or elimination methods. For example, to solve the system of equations x + y = 2 and x - y = 1, we can add the two equations to get 2x = 3, and then divide both sides by 2 to get x = 1.5.
